steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line two cookie sheets with parchment paper or silicone liners.
Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar in a large bowl until smooth and creamy. Beat in eggs and vanilla until fluffy.
Stir together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. Gradually beat into the butter mixture. Stir in oats and raisins. Drop teaspoonfuls of batter 2 inches apart onto the prepared cookie sheets.

Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes, switching racks halfway through. Remove from the oven and let sit on the cookie sheets for 1 to 2 minutes before transferring cookies to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These oatmeal raisin cookies bake up soft and chewy with crispy edges. The whole family will love the flavor and texture of this old standby recipe.

video.description: Oatmeal raisin cookies are a polarizing dessert. Some people love them (like us), while others detest them. But these soft and chewy oatmeal raisin cookies are so good that they just might turn haters into lovers. Don't believe us? Give the oatmeal raisin cookies in this video a try, and see how quickly they disappear.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe! I've read most reviews about the recipe and the most common concerns seem to be that the cookie spreads too thinly when baked and that it is too sweet or bland. I have cut down the sugar to 1/2 cup each of brown and white sugar and added 1/4 tsp ground cloves and 1/4 tsp of ground allspice. Also feel free to add more cinnamon if you like. This made the cookies very flavorful. The trick is, however, mixing the dough by HAND and NOT overworking it. Follow the recipe and incorporate the dry ingredients into the wet in three stages. Do not use a mixer or you will overwork the dough and get flat cookies. I have also soaked the raisins in hot water and drained them in a sieve prior to adding them at the end. Bake the cookies on a cookie sheet at 350 or lower depending on your oven (I baked mine at 325 because my oven was too hot). Regardless at which temperature you bake them, make sure you keep an eye on them after 5-8 minutes and take them out when the edges are golden brown. I had no problems baking these or removing them from the pan. They are moist, flavorful, and delicious. Thanks for a great recipe! This one's a keeper.

Delicious cookie. I tweaked it slightly, though; I used more raisins and soaked them in boiling water first (they were moister and plumper this way), I added a bit more cinnamon, and the batter seemed wet so I ended up adding more flour and oats. However, I would not recommend adding more oats; it was too overpowering. I decided to make monster cookies, hoping they would turn our big and chewy, which they did. I got 20 large cookies from this recipe. Watch the baking time carefully, only adding a minute at a time, if you want chewy cookies.

This recipe came out perfectly for me the first time I tried it. They are a hit with my family. I read most of the reviews here prior to starting. I did soak my raisins which made them extra plump, but I found I did not need to add the extra flour or baking soda, as the dough already had a nice consistency. My cookies did not run at all, and puffed up quite nicely. I cut the white sugar down to 1/2 cup, but kept the brown sugar at 3/4 cup. This did not affect the taste of the cookies, thanks to the raisins, which add natural sweetness. I also added a little extra cinnamon as well as ground star anise (1/2 tsp) to this recipe, which gives a nice flavour. For baking, I rolled spoon-sized amounts of the dough into balls. I turned my oven down to 350, as I found the first batch to be browning a little too quickly on the edges. My cookies needed about 9 minutes, but I had to watch them. They aren't the kind that you can pop in the oven and walk away. Here's a tip: if you want a slightly flatter cookie, press the cookies down with a fork about 1/2 through baking.

I will definitely be making these again!

Great oatmeal raisin cookies, but the default 1 cup of raisins is way, wayyyyy to skimpy. I'm getting about 1 to 1.5 raisins per bite when I should be getting 3. Two cups should be the baseline. Two and a half wouldn't be outrageous. Double the amount of raisins and it's an EXCELLENT recipe.

Easy and delicious. As others suggested, I soaked the raisins in hot water for 15 minutes, added an extra 1/4 cup of flour, and used 2/4 dark brown sugar and 1/4 light brown sugar. Others complained of lack of flavor, so I did a full tsp of cinnamon, 3/4 tsp of salt, 2 tsp of vanilla, and a sprinkling of cloves, allspice, and nutmeg. 9-10 minutes at 360°, and slightly reshaped any thin edges when they came out. Perfect! Best oatmeal raisin cookie ever!

These were sweet, chewy and crunchy around the edges. These are more like lace cookies. I think that the recipe means to call for flour with baking powder in it. If you don’t have that make sure to add 1/2 tsp of Baking powder. I also reduced the raisins by 1/2c, added 1/2 chopped walnuts, more cinnamon, twice the vanilla, and allspice. I notice that they were running so I refrigerated the dough and it helped a little with the spread. I’ll add photos. If you do refrigerate make sure to smush your dough ball a tad to promote an even spread. 9 minutes at 350 was perfect! My family didn’t have any complaints! This is a good base recipe that you can make adjustments to your liking.

I followed the instructions of another reviewer who decreased the sugar to 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar. I mixed everything by hand with a whisk to prevent over-mixing. Substituted chopped prunes for the raisins and added 1/4 tsp ground cloves and 1/4 tsp ground allspice for extra flavor. I folded the rolled oats into the butter/flour mixture until everything was wet and doughey. I then baked at 350F for 12 minutes (checking every 2 minutes at the 8 minute mark to make sure I didn't overbake). The cookies came out perfect--chewy on the inside and crispy on the edges. They're not too sweet if you cut the sugar and so good with a cold glass of milk! I will be making this again.

Really good, Chewy oatmeal cookies! I used an ice cream scoop for the dough, so the cookies were all the same size. I tripled the recipe. I added red river cereal, flax, chia, sunflower, and pumpkin seeds. I also added a can of crushed pineapple(juice included). The first batch spread out a lot, so I chilled the dough for an hour and the second batch spread much less and were thicker than the first batch.

I didn't dislike the taste but it has the tendency to fall apart. So I added 1/4 c flour, 1tsp baking powder. Chilled the mixture before baking. I then left it longer in the oven (I like my cookies a bit crispy on the outside and chewy inside) maybe around 12mins

The only change I made was to add an extra 1/4 cup of flour, after reading the other reviews. I did soak the raisins in hot water for 15 minutes, and put the dough in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. The cookies were totally flat, although the taste was delicious. I was hoping for fluffy cookies. I used parchment paper on fairly good cookie trays, and baked for nine minutes.

I followed the measurements of the recipe except used half butter half Crisco, left out the cinnamon in half the batch and added a cup of chopped pecans. I plopped them on a cookie sheet and flattened them slightly. They were delicious. I baked them at 300 for 7 minutes on bake in my Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven. Perfect.
Did as others recommended. 1/2 cup white sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and more raisins. Very good!
Delicious and super easy!!
These cookies turned out perfectly. I just did mine one day at a time so I didn’t have to switch. They were yummy delicious and my hubby now has a new favorite.
This cookie was fantastic and super easy. I subbed craisins for raisins and they came out beautifully.
Easy

I had originally given this recipe 2 stars because the cookies all came out completely flat with crispy edges and fell apart when picked up. Although I thought they tasted ok, it didn’t “hit the spot” for chewy oatmeal raisin cookies like I was hoping for. However, when I told my husband and his friend to have at the batch, they raved about them, so I bumped it up to 3 stars. I debated on 4 because they liked the flavor so much, but with these crumbling into little pieces every time they’re picked up, they’re a little too impractical for my recipe rotation. I’ve been cleaning up way too many lost cookie edges and crumbs the past couple of days to want to make them again!
I followed the recipe and they turned out really well..
I loved this recipe the cookies turned out delicious. I am making them again today.
I wasn’t happy with the size of the first batch of cookies, so I increased the precooked size from a teaspoon to a tablespoon and they were much better.
